subject: Mutual plan: success signal registry + closure checkpoints
messages:
From: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.ai>
To: Samira Patel <samira.patel@orchidhealth.com>
Cc: marissa.cole@redwood.ai, karthik.iyer@redwood.ai
Date: 2026-10-03T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Draft mutual plan: proposed success signals + checkpoints

Hi Samira —

Thanks again for yesterday's demo. Per our conversation, I've sketched a concise mutual plan focused on how Orchid will evaluate Redwood over the 6-week pilot. The attached workbook (MAP-v1.2.xlsx) contains the registry of success signals, the defensive exit gates we agreed to, and a compact acceptance-test vector matrix.

High level summary (in plain language):
- Objective: Confirm Redwood meets latency SLAs for triage flows and achieves >= 92% semantic recall on the 10k annotated test prompts we discussed.
- Primary success signals: 95th pct latency under 350ms for 1–4 token completions; semantic recall measured against the shared vectors >= 92%.
- Exit gates (automatic): failure to meet latency SLO on two separate weekday windows OR sustained recall <88% after two remediation sprints.
- Acceptance tests: smoke throughput run (1k reqs/min), edge-case prompt set (200 edge cases), and a regression harness against last-mile production prompts. Owners and dates are in the workbook.

Can you review the signal naming/schema and the proposed owners? If this looks right I'll lock it to v1.2 and share with engineering and salesops so we can schedule runs.

Next steps I propose:
1) You confirm or tweak the success thresholds by EOD Mon 10/05.
2) We schedule the first smoke run the week of 10/12 (team availability permitting).
3) If both smoke + edge tests pass, we move to a 2-week live read-only trial before final cutover.

Attaching a short list of things we need from Orchid to proceed:
- A stable dataset snapshot for semantic recall tests (S3 or secure share).
- Contact for network egress testing (Derek was suggested).
- Any regulatory evidence constraints for data retention during the trial.

Thanks — happy to hop on a 20-min call if you prefer to walk this.

—Jonas
Jonas Weber
Senior Solutions Lead, Redwood Inference
j.weber@redwood.ai | +1 415-555-0197

Attachments: MAP-v1.2.xlsx (spreadsheet)

From: Samira Patel <samira.patel@orchidhealth.com>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.ai>
Cc: Derek Long <derek.long@orchidhealth.com>, marissa.cole@redwood.ai
Date: 2026-10-04T08:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Draft mutual plan: proposed success signals + checkpoints

Thanks Jonas — this is really helpful and close to what we discussed. A few quick notes inline: 

- Threshold tweaks: for the semantic recall metric can we use >= 91% as the pass threshold and >= 94% as an aspirational target? We want a realistic bar for go/no-go.
- Exit gates: add a clause for data-privacy discovery — if our compliance team flags an unresolved retention issue within the first two weeks, the pilot pauses until resolved.
- Acceptance tests: can Derek own the egress/network verification and I'll own the edge-case prompt set?

On timing: I can't confirm the dataset snapshot until our infra team completes a short scrub, but target delivery is 10/09. Derek will follow up on network creds.

If you can reflect these edits in v1.3 of the workbook, we'll sign off and schedule the smoke run.

Samira
Samira Patel
Head of Product, Orchid Health
samira.patel@orchidhealth.com

Jonas / Karthik —

Couple tactical items from my side (so we don't miss timeline expectations):
1) Salesops needs the signed MAP doc (v1.3) to provision the dedicated test slot and the PO for reserved capacity. I've added a template clause in the workbook under 'commercial triggers' — please don't expose pricing in the shared copy to Orchid's end users.
2) Engineering needs the 'smoke run' config as a JSON blob (we use this to automate the harness). Can you attach the run spec (target RPS, token limits, payload shapes) when you publish v1.3?
3) Let's keep the first smoke window to 10/12–10/13. If we can't get the dataset by 10/09 we push to 10/19.

I'll coordinate with salesops to spin up test infra once we have the signed sheet. Karthik — can you draft the run spec and drop into the drive link Jonas added?

—Marissa

marissa.cole@redwood.ai

Date: 2026-10-06T15:42:00-07:00
Subject: RE: Draft mutual plan: proposed success signals + checkpoints (v1.3 attached)

Hi Samira —

Thanks for the quick feedback. I've incorporated the threshold changes (semantic recall pass >=91%, aspirational >=94%), and added the compliance pause clause to the exit gates. Attached are two items: the updated MAP workbook (v1.3) and a small archive with the acceptance-test vectors we'll use for local verification.

Engineer's note (run spec summary):
- Smoke run: 1k reqs/min sustained over 10 minutes, target p95 latency <350ms for 1–4 token completions, max tokens capped at 128.
- Edge-case set: 200 prompts covering hallucination triggers, long-context truncation, and entity disambiguation.
- Regression harness: 3 checkpoints (pre-deploy baseline, post-insert, production-readonly).

Owners and dates (excerpt):
- Dataset delivery (Orchid infra): Samira / Derek — target 2026-10-09
- Smoke run (Redwood eng): Karthik / infra — window 2026-10-12 to 2026-10-13
- Acceptance review & signoff (Orchid product): Samira — target 2026-10-20

Samira — when you have a secure share link for the dataset please reply-all. If Orchid signs off on the acceptance tests, Salesops will kick the test capacity and we'll proceed to the live read-only window.

Thanks — attaching files to this thread: acceptance-test-vectors.zip; MAP-v1.3.xlsx

Regards,
Karthik Iyer
Principal Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
